stem.text: One molecule of dodecane, $\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{26}$, is cracked, producing three product molecules, X, Y and Z.
X is a straight chain alkane. Y and Z are straight chain alkenes with different $M_\text{r}$ values.
Which statements about X, Y and Z are correct?

items: If Y and Z are but-1-ene and ethene respectively, X will be hexane.
If X is butane, then Y and Z could both show *cis-trans* isomerism.
